newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares index ends up on support.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares index ends up on support.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed up on Friday mainly due to institutional support for shares with a heavy index weighting following falls in the past three days, brokers said.
The index rose 0.947 points or 1.53 percent to 62.837 points, on volume of 20.9 million shares worth $8.8 million against $4.8 million on Thursday.

Brokers said institutional support for market giants such as property developer Lujiazui and Shanghai Diesel Engine triggered some follow-up buying, which made trading volume increase sharply from Thursday.
"But today's rises have improved the technical charts, which will help the market to move steadily around current levels in the short term," he added.
Of 43 B shares, 41 traded, with 22 up, six flat and 13 down.
Hua Xin Cement became the star on institutional buying, jumping $0.022 or 9.56 percent to $0.252 on today's heaviest volume of 3.8 million shares.
Shanghai's A share market was up on active institutional buying in selective stocks, but trading remained sluggish with follow-up buying limited, brokers said.

The A index ended up 4.771 points or 0.50 percent to 959.946 points, on volume of 194.9 million shares worth 2.1 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 29.389 points or 1.21 percent to 2464.035 points.
Shanghai Steel Tube was the star, jumping 0.56 yuan or 8.06 percent to 7.50 yuan on volume of 1.8 million shares.
"Institutions with large positions in hand bought index-weighting market shares to push the index up," one broker said. "That attracted some domestic investors to follow up."
Market giant Shanghai Diesel Engine rose $0.018 or 3.73 percent to $0.500 on volume of 973,620 shares.
Market barometer Lujiazui gained $0.030 or 3.70 percent to $0.840 on volume of 2.1 million shares.

"The rebound is likely to be short-lived with heavy liquidation expected at high levels given the lack of fresh capital flowing into the market," a second broker said. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
